text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive blocks like headers and nav bars, cutting navigation time from seconds to milliseconds. The trade-off is one extra DOM node per page, which adds negligible weight but guarantees universal access for anyone who can’t use a mouse.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link entirely if it’s hidden until focused—it becomes visual noise, not a tool. A better alternative is an always-visible skip link styled to match the page’s color scheme, so it’s discoverable without sacrificing contrast. Settle it with user testing: track if keyboard users can find and use it within 3 seconds in a live prototype.

name: Ramp
text:
Add an always-visible, high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. This guarantees sighted keyboard users see it immediately, solving the discoverability problem without relying on focus states. The trade-off is a small visual element that stays on screen, but its utility for navigation speed outweighs the minimal clutter.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users treating the always-visible skip link as visual clutter, especially on dense pages where it competes with primary content. A better alternative is a skip link that appears on keyboard focus but uses a high-contrast outline—like a thick border—so it’s unmistakable when needed but doesn’t persist. Settle it with user testing: measure if sighted keyboard users can spot and use it without training.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **focus-triggered skip link**—high-contrast, full-width, and triggered by keyboard tab—with a fallback always-visible outline for sighted keyboard users. Result: a skip link that’s discoverable, fast, and unobtrusive. Owner: accessibility-w1.
